rv.q: It’s Just Like Coming to Church” feels rather like a balm in a time of pandemic and war, when the awful news is so relentless we literally had to make up words to describe it, like “doomscrolling.
This production is a wonderful way to welcome back Jackie Taylor’s inspiring and entertaining Black Ensemble Theater.
It’s an energizing and participatory homage to the Black church experience, which as the cast shares, “ain’t no ‘I’m just gonna sit here and listen kind of place.’”
For lovers of Gospel Music and powerful voices, there are sixteen treasures in this play to savor.
What is welcome is the return of a troupe that, when they sing, is absolutely heaven.
Playgoers anticipating Black Ensemble Theater’s customary splendor may be disappointed at the modesty of its first post-pandemic venture.
Jackie Taylor’s ‘It’s Just Like Coming To Church’ falls in line with the usual fun with no thrills musicals Black Ensemble is known for producing.
This production is one of the most joyous events that you can attend these days, and you’ll hear some phenomenal music along the way.

cn.t: Critics hail this joyous, energizing return as an uplifting celebration of community and the Black church experience, with phenomenal music spanning gospel to hip-hop and powerful messages of self-love and forgiveness.
